title: Lenny Adapter Binary Protocol (JSONL)
description: Newline-delimited JSON exchanged on stdin/stdout between the adapter sidecar and the agent binary inside a Lenny pod. The adapter receives lines on stdin (inbound) and reads lines from stdout (outbound). Each line is a single JSON object discriminated by `type`. The adapter↔runtime CH-RUNTIMEOPS frames (checkpoint_request, interrupt_request, credentials_rotated, deadline_approaching, and their runtime replies) travel on the intra-pod runtime-ops Unix socket, are schematized in schemas/runtime-ops-events.schema.json, and are out of scope here. The stdin/stdout message schemas are stated by spec/28_communication-channels.md §28.5.3, the CH-MSGSOCK card; the messageEnvelope definition is stated by the MessageEnvelope unified message format heading in spec/15_external-api-surface.md §15.4.

messageEnvelope.title: message
messageEnvelope.description: Inbound content delivery from gateway → adapter → agent. The unified envelope used for client prompts, inter-session messages, and platform-injected control text. See spec/15_external-api-surface.md §15.4.

schemaVersion.description: Gateway-injected at write time. Immutable. Consumers MUST forward-read.

id.description: ULID-like message id (msg_ prefix). Tenant-unique. Duplicate ids reject with 400 DUPLICATE_MESSAGE_ID.

inReplyTo.description: Optional reply-to message id for DAG threading and lenny/request_input routing.

threadId.description: Optional thread label. v1 has an implicit single thread per session.

delivery.description: Interrupt behavior. `immediate` preempts running work; `queued` waits for the agent to drain.

delegationDepth.description: Gateway-injected hop count in the delegation tree. Informational.

sessionId.description: The session this frame is addressed to. The adapter populates it on every session-scoped frame on every pod, whatever the pool's `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions`, so an empty address is as non-conforming as an absent one on this leg. `from.id` separately names the sending session, which may be a different session; delivery follows `sessionId`.

input.description: Message content as a list of MessagePart objects.

from.description: Sender context. Adapter-injects this; runtimes MUST NOT set it.

kind.description: Closed enum. Determines the expected shape of `id`.

id.description: Identifier whose shape depends on kind. client: `client_{opaque}`. agent: `sess_{session_id}`. system: literal `lenny-gateway`. external: `conn_{connector_id}`. When kind is `agent` this names the sending session, which may differ from the `sessionId` the frame is addressed to.

heartbeat.title: heartbeat
heartbeat.description: Inbound liveness ping from adapter. Agent must respond with heartbeat_ack within 10s or the adapter ends the session's stream; the runtime process receives no signal. A protocol-level frame: it carries no per-session identifier and is outside the session addressing rule stated by spec/28_communication-channels.md §28.5.3.

heartbeat_ack.title: heartbeat_ack
heartbeat_ack.description: Outbound acknowledgement of an inbound heartbeat. A protocol-level frame: it carries no per-session identifier and is outside the session addressing rule stated by spec/28_communication-channels.md §28.5.3.

session_start.title: session_start
session_start.description: Inbound frame that opens a session on the runtime and carries the session's own context. The adapter writes it once for each start and each resume of the session, and on the connection or loop that carries the session it precedes every other frame addressed to the session. A runtime that keeps per-session context creates the session's context from it and answers with session_started; a runtime that has opened CH-RUNTIMEOPS answers every session_start with session_started. A runtime that keeps no per-session context and opens no CH-RUNTIMEOPS connection may ignore it. A runtime ignores a session_start for a session it already holds, except that it answers it with session_started again. See spec/28_communication-channels.md §28.5.3, the CH-MSGSOCK card.

sessionId.description: The session the frame opens. The adapter populates it on every pod.

startId.description: Identifies this write of the frame. The adapter gives each session_start it writes on the pod a value distinct from every other it has written there, so the acknowledgement of an earlier start of the same session is not read as this start's.

credentialsPath.description: Absolute path to this session's credential file, /run/lenny/slots/{sessionId}/credentials.json. The adapter writes the file before it writes this frame and rewrites it in place on a rotation for this session. Present whenever the adapter provisioned a credential file for the session and absent otherwise; the adapter never writes an empty path, and a runtime given no path loads no credential bundle for the session.

experimentContext.description: Experiment enrollment context for this session. Absent or null when the session is not enrolled in any experiment.

inherited.description: True when the enrollment was propagated from a parent session through delegation.

tracingContext.description: Opaque map of non-sensitive tracing identifiers propagated from the parent runtime through delegation. Absent or null for a top-level session.

llm.description: LLM provider configuration for the session. Absent or null when the session has no active LLM credential lease.

deliveryMode.description: The credential delivery mode active for this session's LLM provider pool.

dialect.description: The dialect the runtime's LLM SDK speaks to the LLM Proxy, openai or anthropic. Present in proxy mode and omitted in direct mode.

apiKeyEnv.description: Canonical environment variable name the runtime's LLM SDK reads for its API key. The runtime supplies the session's lease token as that session's key rather than setting the variable in its own process environment.

headers.description: Header names and string values the runtime's LLM SDK sends to the LLM Proxy in proxy mode. Omitted when no header is advertised.

session_started.title: session_started
session_started.description: Outbound acknowledgement of a session_start. A runtime that keeps per-session context writes it after it has created the session's context, and a runtime that has opened CH-RUNTIMEOPS writes it for every session_start it reads. The adapter consumes it and relays it to no Attach stream, and it drops one whose startId is not that of the start waiting for the session. See spec/28_communication-channels.md §28.5.3, the CH-MSGSOCK card.

sessionId.description: The session whose session_start the frame answers. The runtime echoes the identifier of the session_start it answers.

startId.description: The runtime echoes the startId of the session_start it answers, including a repeated one.

error.description: Present when the runtime failed to create the session's context, and absent otherwise. The object a response error carries.

session_end.title: session_end
session_end.description: Inbound frame that releases a session on the runtime. It ends the start of the latest session_start the runtime read for the session, and the runtime releases the context that start creates and keeps serving the pod's other sessions. It is not acknowledged and carries no deadline. A runtime ignores a session_end for a session it does not hold. When the connection or loop that carries a session ends, no session_end follows. See spec/28_communication-channels.md §28.5.3, the CH-MSGSOCK card.

sessionId.description: The session the frame releases. The adapter populates it on every pod.

shutdown.title: shutdown
shutdown.description: Inbound process-scoped graceful-shutdown signal. The adapter never writes it at a session boundary; a session's end is session_end. The agent must finish its current work and exit within deadline_ms or receive SIGTERM.

deadline_ms.description: Milliseconds the agent has to exit before SIGTERM.

tool_call.title: tool_call
tool_call.description: Outbound request to invoke an adapter-local tool (read_file, write_file, list_dir, delete_file) or a platform MCP tool (lenny/...). When the call requires explicit user approval before execution, the runtime sets `approvalRequired: true`; the adapter then publishes the §7.2 `tool_use_requested` SSE event and blocks the call on a POST /v1/sessions/{id}/tool-use/{tool_call_id}/approve|deny resolution before forwarding the call.

name.description: Tool name. Adapter-local: read_file, write_file, list_dir, delete_file. Platform MCP: lenny/<tool>.

arguments.description: Tool-specific parameters. Validated against the tool's inputSchema.

approvalRequired.description: When true, the adapter records a §7.2 KindToolUse interaction, publishes a `tool_use_requested(tool_call_id, tool, args)` SSE event on the session's event stream, and blocks the tool invocation until the user resolves via POST /v1/sessions/{id}/tool-use/{tool_call_id}/approve|deny. A denial returns the tool a structured `tool_result` carrying `isError: true` and the deny reason; an approval forwards the call. Absent or false means the call executes immediately (no approval gate).

sessionId.description: The session this frame is addressed to. The runtime echoes the identifier it was handed, on every pod. An absent identifier resolves to the receiving stream's own binding on a pod holding at most one slot, and on a pod holding more than one slot it is rejected and relayed to no stream.

tool_result.title: tool_result
tool_result.description: Inbound result for a prior tool_call. The id matches the originating tool_call.id. Results with no matching call are dropped and logged.

content.description: Result content as a list of MessagePart objects.

sessionId.description: The session this frame is addressed to. The adapter populates it on every pod, whatever the pool's `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions`, so an empty address is as non-conforming as an absent one on this leg.

response.title: response
response.description: Outbound task completion with the final output. Either `output` (canonical) or `text` (shorthand for a single text part).

output.description: Complete task output as a list of MessagePart objects.

text.description: Shorthand for text-only responses. The adapter normalizes this to a single text MessagePart in `output`.

error.description: Structured task failure, maps to TaskResult.error.

sessionId.description: The session this frame is addressed to. The runtime echoes the identifier it was handed, on every pod. An absent identifier resolves to the receiving stream's own binding on a pod holding at most one slot, and on a pod holding more than one slot it is rejected and relayed to no stream.

status.title: status
status.description: Outbound optional status update, surfaced to the client as a low-priority signal. A session-scoped frame: it is addressed to the session named by `sessionId` and relayed to that session's stream alone.

state.description: Status label (for example: thinking, analyzing, calling_tool).

sessionId.description: The session this frame is addressed to. The runtime echoes the identifier it was handed, on every pod. An absent identifier resolves to the receiving stream's own binding on a pod holding at most one slot, and on a pod holding more than one slot it is rejected and relayed to no stream.

set_tracing_context.title: set_tracing_context
set_tracing_context.description: Outbound distributed-tracing context propagation. The agent declares its trace identifiers so the gateway can stitch them into the platform trace and forward to delegated children.

context.description: Opaque tracing context. Typical keys: langsmith_run_id, otel_trace_id, otel_span_id, tracestate.

sessionId.description: The session this frame is addressed to. The runtime echoes the identifier it was handed, on every pod. An absent identifier resolves to the receiving stream's own binding on a pod holding at most one slot, and on a pod holding more than one slot it is rejected and relayed to no stream.
